terms.definition: The special method Python calls right after creating an instance, used to set its starting attributes.
Randomly splitting users into a control and a variant, then using statistics to check whether a metric really differs.
A class that cannot be instantiated and declares methods subclasses must implement, using the abc module.
The fraction of predictions that are correct. It can mislead when classes are imbalanced.
A non-linear function applied to a neuron's output, which is what lets a network learn more than straight-line relationships.
A program that lets a language model decide on actions, call tools, observe the results and repeat until the task is done.
Two names referring to the same object, so a change made through one name shows up through the other.
terms.example: b = a  # b is not a copy of a

terms.definition: Application Programming Interface: a defined way for one program to ask another to do something, such as a web API accepting HTTP requests.
A FastAPI object for grouping related endpoints in a module, which the main app then includes.
The standard-library module for declaring a command-line program's arguments and generating parsing, validation and --help output.
The actual value you pass to a function when you call it.
The standard library for cooperative concurrency: one thread runs many tasks and switches between them while they wait on I/O.
Writing to a temporary file and then renaming it over the target, so readers see either the old or the new file, never a half-written one.
A mechanism where each token computes a weighted mix of the other tokens' information, with the weights learned from how relevant they are.
A piece of data stored on an object or class and read with dot notation.
Proving who you are, for example with a password or token. Authorization is deciding what you may then do.
terms.example: log in with email and password

terms.definition: Deciding what an already identified user is allowed to do.
PyTorch's automatic differentiation: it records tensor operations so .backward() can compute gradients for you.
Running a pipeline for past dates it missed, or for a new logic version, to fill in historical results.
terms.example: run the daily job for last month

terms.definition: Work scheduled to run after the response has been sent, so the client does not wait for it.
Computing the gradient of the loss with respect to every weight by applying the chain rule backward from the output to the input.
Building a solution step by step and undoing the last choice whenever it leads to a dead end.
Representing a text by how many times each vocabulary word appears, ignoring word order.
The simplest input of a recursive function, answered directly without another recursive call. Without it the recursion never ends.
A small group of training samples processed together for one weight update.
A rule for updating a probability with new evidence: P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B).
Breadth-first search: visit all nodes at distance 1, then distance 2 and so on, using a queue. It finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
Simple models tend to have high bias (systematic error), flexible models high variance (sensitivity to the training sample). Good models balance the two.
terms.example: shallow tree = high bias; deep tree = high variance

terms.definition: A way to describe how an algorithm's running time or memory grows with input size n, ignoring constant factors.
Finding a value in a sorted list by repeatedly halving the search range, in O(log n) time.
A tree in which each node has at most two children, usually called left and right.
An array of True/False values used to select the elements where the condition holds.
The AWS SDK for Python, used to call AWS services such as EC2 and S3 from code.
NumPy's rule for combining arrays of different shapes by stretching size-1 dimensions to match.
Sending a small share of real traffic to a new version first, and rolling back if its metrics look worse.
Prompting a model to write out its reasoning step by step before the final answer, which often improves results on multi-step problems.
Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery: automatically testing every change and, if it passes, building and releasing it.
A guard that stops calling a repeatedly failing service for a while, then lets a trial call through to see if it has recovered.
A blueprint that defines the attributes and methods its objects will have. Calling the class creates an instance.
Predicting which category an item belongs to, such as spam or not spam.
A method marked with @classmethod that receives the class (cls) instead of an instance. It is often used for alternative constructors.
An inner function that remembers variables from the enclosing function even after that function has returned.
terms.example: def make_adder(n): return lambda x: x + n

terms.definition: Grouping items so that those in the same group are more similar to each other than to other groups.
A program you run from a terminal by typing its name and arguments. In Python the arguments arrive in sys.argv or through argparse.
Building an object out of other objects it holds (has-a) instead of inheriting from them (is-a).
terms.example: self.engine = Engine()  # a Car has an Engine

terms.definition: The relationship between inputs and the correct answer changes, so the same input now deserves a different prediction.
The probability of an event given that another event has already happened, written P(A | B).
When a running system's real configuration gradually differs from what is declared or intended.
terms.example: prod differs from the repo file

terms.definition: A table counting predictions against true labels: true positives, false positives, false negatives and true negatives.
A running, isolated process created from an image, sharing the host's kernel but with its own filesystem and network view.
An object used with the with statement that sets something up on entry and always cleans up on exit, even after an error.
A neural network for images that slides small learned filters across the input to detect patterns like edges and shapes.
The object returned by calling an async def function. It runs only when awaited or scheduled on an event loop.
A number from -1 to 1 showing how strongly two variables move together in a straight-line way. It does not prove one causes the other.
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: a browser rule that blocks a web page from calling another origin's API unless the server allows it with special headers.
The cosine of the angle between two vectors: 1 means the same direction, 0 unrelated, -1 opposite. It compares direction, not length.
A dict subclass from collections that counts how often items occur and can list the most common.
The longest chain of dependent tasks in a pipeline, which sets the minimum time the whole run can take.
A scheduler for recurring jobs, configured with five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week.
Splitting the data into k parts, training on k-1 and testing on the remaining one in turn, then averaging the k scores.
Directed Acyclic Graph: tasks as nodes and dependencies as one-way arrows with no cycles. Pipelines use it to define run order.
An agreed and checkable description of a dataset's schema and rules, such as column types and allowed ranges, that producers promise and consumers can validate.
The distribution of the model's inputs in production shifts away from what it was trained on.
terms.example: ages in live traffic skew younger than in training data

terms.definition: When information the model would not have at prediction time (such as test data or the future) slips into training, making scores look better than reality.
terms.example: scaling on all data before splitting

terms.definition: A short-lived unit of work with the database that tracks changes and commits or rolls them back together.
A decorator that generates __init__, __repr__ and __eq__ for a class from its annotated fields.
pandas' two-dimensional table with labelled rows (index) and named columns.
A PyTorch helper that loads a dataset in shuffled batches for the training loop.
The line or surface where a classifier switches from one predicted class to another.
A model that predicts by asking a chain of yes/no questions about features, each split sending a sample down a branch to a leaf.
A function that takes a function and returns a wrapped or replaced version, applied with @ above the definition.
A value a parameter takes when the caller omits it. The default is created once at definition time, so a mutable default is shared between calls.
Having the framework build and hand a function the objects it needs, such as a database session, instead of the function creating them. FastAPI does this with Depends().
The rate at which a function's output changes as its input changes; the slope of its curve at a point.
Depth-first search: explore as far as possible along one path before backing up, using recursion or a stack.
terms.example: visit(node); for n in node.next: dfs(n)

terms.definition: A collection of key-value pairs where you look up a value by its key. Keys must be hashable and unique.
Reducing the number of features while keeping as much useful information as possible.
A tool that packages an application with its dependencies into an image that runs the same way as an isolated container on any machine.
A string as the first statement of a function, class or module that documents it. Available as __doc__ and shown by help().
Multiply two vectors element by element and add the results. It measures how strongly they point the same way.
A change over time in the data or in the data-to-label relationship that quietly makes a deployed model less accurate.
terms.example: average order value doubles after a new market launch

terms.definition: Judging an object by the methods it has rather than its class: if it has the method you need, it works.
terms.example: anything with .read() can be used like a file

terms.definition: Solving a problem by breaking it into overlapping subproblems and storing each answer so it is computed only once.
terms.example: fib with a table of earlier results

terms.definition: Plot the k-means error (inertia) against k and pick the k where the curve bends and gains flatten out.
terms.example: look for the bend in the inertia plot

terms.definition: A list of numbers (a dense vector) representing a word, token or document, learned so that similar meanings sit close together.
Bundling data with the methods that use it and controlling outside access, so internal details can change without breaking users.
One URL path plus HTTP method that a server handles with a function.
A combination of several models whose joint prediction is usually better than any single one.
A named setting supplied to a process by its surroundings, commonly used for configuration and secrets that must not live in code.
One complete pass of the training loop over the whole training dataset.
The amount of failure an SLO allows, which is 1 minus the target. Spending it too fast is a signal to slow down changes.
The scheduler in asyncio that runs tasks and resumes each one when the thing it awaited is ready.
An error object raised when something goes wrong at runtime. If nothing catches it the program stops and prints a traceback.
The number a program returns to its caller when it ends. 0 means success and any other value signals an error.
Recording each training run's parameters, metrics, code version and artefacts so runs can be compared and reproduced.
Waiting longer after each failed retry, usually doubling the delay, so a struggling service is not hammered.
A string literal starting with f whose {braces} are evaluated as Python expressions and formatted into the text.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number that is low unless both are reasonably high.
A Python web framework for building APIs from type-annotated functions, with automatic validation and interactive docs.
Creating or transforming input columns so a model can learn from them more easily.
Turning categorical values into indices of a fixed-size vector with a hash function, so no vocabulary must be stored and unseen values still map somewhere.
A score for how much each input feature contributed to a model's predictions.
The output grid a kernel produces, showing where in the input its pattern was detected.
Rescaling features to comparable ranges. Standardisation subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation.
Putting a few worked examples in the prompt so the model copies the pattern. With zero examples it is called zero-shot.
Continuing to train a pretrained model on your own smaller dataset so it specialises in your task.
terms.example: start from BERT, train on your reviews

terms.definition: A filter that allows or blocks network traffic according to rules. A stateful firewall tracks connections and automatically allows replies to allowed requests.
In pytest, a reusable setup function whose return value is injected into tests by name.
A number type stored in binary with limited precision, so many decimal fractions are only approximated.
Passing inputs through the network layer by layer to compute the output and the loss.
A named, reusable block of code that takes inputs (arguments), runs its body, and hands back a result with return.
terms.example: def add(a, b): return a + b

terms.definition: A function that uses yield to produce values one at a time, keeping its state between them, so big sequences never sit in memory at once.
The vector of partial derivatives of a function with respect to each input. It points in the direction of steepest increase.
An ensemble method that adds small models one after another, each trained to correct the errors of the ones before it.
An optimisation method that repeatedly steps opposite to the gradient of the loss to make the loss smaller.
A set of nodes connected by edges, commonly stored as an adjacency list mapping each node to its neighbours.
A regex quantifier that matches as much text as possible. Adding ? makes it lazy, matching as little as possible.
An algorithm that always takes the best-looking choice at the moment. It is fast but only correct for some problems.
terms.example: give the largest coin that fits

terms.definition: Trying every combination of listed hyperparameter values, scoring each with cross-validation, and keeping the best.
Split rows into groups by a column, apply an aggregate to each group, and combine the results.
A limit that keeps a system safe, such as a maximum step count, an allow-list of tools, or output validation.
A structure that stores key-value pairs and finds a key in O(1) on average by hashing it. Python's dict is a hash map.
An object with a hash value that never changes during its life, which lets it be a dict key or a set member. Lists are not hashable.
A simple endpoint or probe that reports whether a service is alive and ready, used by load balancers and orchestrators.
A tree-based structure that always gives you the smallest (min-heap) item in O(log n). Python's heapq implements it on a list.
A bar chart that counts how many values fall in each range (bin), showing the shape of a distribution.
The request/response protocol of the web. A client sends a method, URL, headers and optional body; the server replies with a status code, headers and body.
A name: value line of metadata sent with a request or response, such as Content-Type or Authorization.
The verb of an HTTP request: GET reads, POST creates or triggers, PUT replaces, PATCH partly updates and DELETE removes.
A three-digit number in a response: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.
The exception you raise in FastAPI to stop and return an HTTP error response with a chosen status code and message.
A setting you choose before training, such as tree depth or learning rate, as opposed to parameters the model learns.
Using different thresholds to trigger and to clear an alert, so a value hovering near the line does not make it flip on and off.
AWS Identity and Access Management: the service whose policies state which identities may perform which actions on which resources.
Doing it twice has the same effect as doing it once. Idempotent steps are safe to retry.
terms.example: PUT /users/7 with the same body twice

terms.definition: An object whose contents cannot be changed after it is created. Strings, tuples and numbers are immutable.
Using a trained model to make predictions on new data, as opposed to training it.
Defining a class that builds on another (its parent), reusing its methods and attributes and adding or replacing some.
A small random amount added to retry delays so many clients do not all retry at the same instant.
A text format for nested data built from objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null. json.loads turns it into Python dicts and lists.
JSON Web Token: a signed string of header, payload and signature that carries claims such as the user id. It is signed, not encrypted, so never put secrets in it.
A clustering algorithm that repeats two steps: assign each point to the nearest of k centres, then move each centre to the mean of its points.
The small grid of learned weights that a convolution slides across an input to produce a feature map.
An argument passed by parameter name (name=value), so order does not matter. A function can collect extras with **kwargs.
The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test compares two samples by the largest gap between their cumulative distributions, to judge whether they come from the same distribution.
A system that runs and manages containers across many machines, keeping the desired number running and restarting failures.
A small anonymous function written as a single expression.
A very large transformer trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next token, which lets it generate and transform text.
The time between sending a request and receiving its response.
Layer 4 balancers route using IP addresses and ports (TCP/UDP) only. Layer 7 balancers read the HTTP request, so they can route by path or header.
The step size in gradient descent. Too large and training overshoots or diverges; too small and it is very slow.
A model that predicts a number as a weighted sum of the features plus a constant, fitted by minimising squared error.
An ordered, mutable sequence of items, written in square brackets.
A compact expression that builds a list by looping over an iterable, optionally filtering items.
terms.example: [n * n for n in range(5) if n % 2 == 0]

terms.definition: A component that spreads incoming requests across several servers and avoids unhealthy ones.
A time-ordered record of events a program writes, one line per event, used to debug and monitor.
The standard library's system for recording events with severity levels (DEBUG to CRITICAL) to handlers such as the console or a file.
A classification model that passes a linear combination of features through a sigmoid to output a probability between 0 and 1.
A number that measures how wrong a model's predictions are. Training tries to make it small.
A cache that, when full, removes the Least Recently Used item first.
Long Short-Term Memory: an RNN whose gates decide what to forget, store and output, which helps it remember over long sequences.
A rectangular grid of numbers with rows and columns. A dataset is often a matrix with one row per sample and one column per feature.
Combining two matrices where each result entry is the dot product of a row from the first and a column from the second. Inner sizes must match.
The sum of the values divided by how many there are. It is pulled by extreme values.
The middle value once the data is sorted. It is barely affected by outliers.
Caching a function's results by its arguments so repeated calls are instant.
Combine two tables sideways by matching rows on key columns, like a SQL join.
A stable divide-and-conquer sort that splits the list, sorts both halves and merges them, in O(n log n) time.
A function defined inside a class. Called on an object, it receives that object automatically as its first argument, self.
The order in which Python searches a class and its parents for a method. Shown by ClassName.__mro__.
A small, independently deployed service that does one job and talks to others over the network.
Code that wraps every request and response of an app, used for logging, timing or adding headers.
Cells with no data, shown as NaN in pandas. You must find them and decide whether to drop or fill them.
A small class that adds one capability to other classes through multiple inheritance and is not meant to stand alone.
A short document describing a model's intended use, training data, metrics and limitations.
A store of versioned models with stages such as staging and production, so you know which model is deployed and can roll back.
Saving a trained model object to a file so another process can load and reuse it. Only load pickle files you trust, because loading can run code.
A Python file whose names (functions, classes, variables) can be reused in other files with import.
An object that can be changed in place after creation, such as a list, dict or set. Other names for the same object see the change.
A run of n consecutive words or characters, used to capture local word order.
Finding and labelling names of people, places, organisations and similar items in text.
A regex group given a name with (?P<name>...) so you can read the match by name instead of number.
A model made of layers of simple units, each computing a weighted sum plus an activation. Stacked layers can learn complex patterns.
The training task of a language model: given the tokens so far, output a probability for every possible next token.
A measure of a vector's length. The L2 (Euclidean) norm is the square root of the sum of squares.
A symmetric bell-shaped distribution described by its mean and standard deviation. About 68% of values fall within one standard deviation of the mean.
The core Python library for fast n-dimensional arrays and vectorised maths.
An authorisation standard where a client presents an access token, often in an Authorization: Bearer header, instead of a password.
A value built from a class, bundling data (attributes) with behaviour (methods). Each instance has its own attribute values.
The algorithm that updates model weights from their gradients, such as SGD or Adam.
Object-Relational Mapper: a library that maps database tables to Python classes and rows to objects, so you query with Python instead of raw SQL.
When a model memorises quirks and noise of its training data, so it scores well on training data but poorly on new data.
Extra values (usually zeros) added around an input's border so a convolution keeps the output size or reaches the edges.
Returning a long result in pages, with a token or link to fetch the next page, so you must loop until none is left.
A Python library for tabular data built around the DataFrame and Series.
A name in a function definition that receives a value when the function is called.
terms.example: def greet(name):  # name is the parameter

terms.definition: Storing a one-way, salted hash of a password instead of the password itself, so a database leak does not reveal them.
A variable part of the URL path, declared in braces and passed to the function.
A standard-library module that represents file paths as objects, with operators and methods instead of string juggling.
Principal Component Analysis: projects data onto a few new axes that capture as much of the variance as possible, reducing the number of features.
The value below which a given percent of observations fall. p95 latency means 95% of requests were faster. Percentiles show slow tails that an average hides.
Python's package installer, which downloads libraries from PyPI into the current environment.
In scikit-learn, a chain of preprocessing steps and a final model that behaves like a single model and is fitted and applied together.
A summary table that reshapes data so one column's values become the columns, with an aggregate in each cell.
The smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes: one or more containers that share a network address and storage.
Joining each event to the feature values as they were at that event's time, not later values, to avoid leaking the future into training.
terms.example: use the balance from before the loan decision

terms.definition: Different classes providing the same method name, so code can call it without caring which class the object is.
Downsampling that summarises each small window by its maximum (max pooling) or average, shrinking the feature map.
Extra position information added to token embeddings, because attention alone has no sense of word order.
Of the items the model flagged as positive, the fraction that really are positive: TP / (TP + FP).
A model already trained on a large dataset that you download and reuse instead of training from scratch.
The text you give a language model to tell it what to do.
A method exposed like an attribute, letting you compute or validate a value while callers keep using plain dot access.

Population Stability Index: a score comparing a feature's binned distribution now versus a baseline, summing (actual% - expected%) * ln(actual% / expected%). Below about 0.1 is usually read as stable and above 0.25 as a major shift.
A library that validates data against Python type annotations and converts it into typed objects; FastAPI uses it for request and response bodies.
The standard project configuration file in TOML format, holding a Python project's name, version, dependencies and tool settings.
A popular Python testing framework that finds test_* functions, uses plain assert statements, and provides fixtures.
An optional key=value pair after the ? in a URL, used for filters and options.
A divide-and-conquer sort that partitions around a pivot and sorts each side. It averages O(n log n) but can degrade to O(n^2).
An ensemble of many decision trees, each trained on a random sample of rows and features, whose predictions are averaged or voted.
The starting value of a pseudo-random number generator. The same seed gives the same sequence, which makes 'random' steps repeatable.
An agent pattern that alternates Reasoning (thought), Acting (a tool call) and Observing the result.
Of the items that really are positive, the fraction the model found: TP / (TP + FN).
A network for sequences that reads one item at a time and carries a hidden state forward as its memory.
A function solving a problem by calling itself on a smaller piece of it. It needs a base case to stop.
terms.example: def fact(n): return 1 if n <= 1 else n * fact(n - 1)

terms.definition: Predicting a number, such as a price, rather than a category.
A compact pattern language for matching and extracting text.
Rectified Linear Unit: an activation that outputs the input if it is positive and zero otherwise, max(0, x).
Being able to rerun an experiment with the same code, data, seeds and environment and get the same result.
In Kubernetes, a request is the amount of CPU or memory reserved for a container and a limit is the most it may use.
A model declared on an endpoint describing the shape of its response, which FastAPI uses to validate and filter the output.
Retrieve relevant documents first, put them into the prompt, then let the model generate an answer grounded in them.
A load-balancing method that sends each new request to the next server in a fixed rotation.
terms.example: A, B, C, A, B, C

terms.definition: The region of code where a name can be seen. Python looks in the local, enclosing, global and built-in scopes in that order.
terms.example: a name assigned inside a function is local to it

terms.definition: A cloud firewall attached to instances that lists which network traffic is allowed in and out.
By convention the first parameter of an instance method: the object the method was called on.
Finding documents by meaning: embed the query and the documents and rank by vector similarity instead of matching keywords.
A MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version scheme: increment MAJOR for breaking changes, MINOR for compatible features, PATCH for fixes.
An unordered collection of unique, hashable items with fast membership tests and set operations such as union and intersection.
Running a new model on a copy of live traffic without using its answers, to compare it with the current model safely.
terms.example: v2 predicts silently; users get v1

terms.definition: and / or stop evaluating as soon as the result is decided, so the right-hand side may never run.
terms.example: user and user.name  # skips .name when user is None

terms.definition: The S-shaped function 1 / (1 + e^-z) that squashes any number into the range 0 to 1.
Service Level Indicator: a measured number describing service quality, such as the share of requests answered under 300 ms.
Taking part of a sequence with start:stop:step. The stop index is excluded and the result is a new object.
A technique that keeps a moving range over a sequence and updates its total as it slides, instead of recomputing each range.
terms.example: best sum of any 3 in a row

terms.definition: Service Level Objective: the target value set for an SLI over a period, such as 99.9% of requests succeeding in a month.
A function that turns a vector of scores into probabilities that are positive and add up to 1.
A method with double underscores on both sides, such as __repr__ or __len__, which Python calls to implement built-in behaviour.
The main Python SQL toolkit and ORM.
The square root of the variance, in the same units as the data.
The collection of modules that ships with Python, such as math, json, pathlib and collections.
A method marked with @staticmethod that receives neither the instance nor the class; it is a plain function grouped inside the class.
A very common word such as 'the' or 'and' that is often removed before analysis because it carries little meaning.
How many positions a convolution or pooling window moves each step. A larger stride gives a smaller output.
An immutable sequence of characters used for text. Slicing and methods return new strings instead of changing the old one.
The standard-library module for starting other programs from Python and capturing their output and exit code.
Returns a proxy to the parent class so a child method can call the parent's version.
Communication where the caller waits for the reply before continuing. Asynchronous means it hands off the work and carries on.
terms.example: an HTTP call that blocks until the response

terms.definition: Transmission Control Protocol: a connection-based protocol that delivers bytes reliably and in order, retransmitting lost data.
A sampling setting that divides the model's scores before softmax. Low values make output more predictable; high values make it more varied.
PyTorch's n-dimensional array. It works like a NumPy array but can live on a GPU and track gradients.
An infrastructure-as-code tool where you declare cloud resources in files. terraform plan shows the changes before they are applied.
A FastAPI test helper that sends requests to your app in-process, without starting a real server.
Term Frequency times Inverse Document Frequency: a word weight that is high for words frequent in a document but rare across the collection.
A limit on how long to wait for something before giving up, so a slow dependency cannot hang the caller forever.
One unit of text as a model sees it, often a word or a piece of a word, mapped to an integer id.
A rate limiter that holds up to a fixed number of tokens refilled at a steady rate. Each request spends a token and is refused when none are left.
Splitting text into tokens: words, subwords or characters that a model treats as its basic units.
A strict, typed configuration format of key = value lines and [tables], readable in Python with tomllib.
A model replying with a structured request to run a named tool with arguments; your code runs it and returns the result to the model.
Sampling the next token only from the k most probable candidates, cutting off unlikely ones.
An ordering of a DAG's nodes in which every node comes after everything it depends on. Kahn's algorithm builds it by repeatedly removing nodes with no unmet dependencies.
The report Python prints for an uncaught exception, listing the chain of calls that led to it with the most recent call last.
A mismatch between how features are computed at training time and at serving time, so the model sees different inputs in production.
terms.example: trained on cleaned text but served raw text

terms.definition: Holding back part of the data that the model never trains on, so you can measure how it performs on new examples.
terms.example: X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y)

terms.definition: Adjusting a model's internal numbers (parameters) so its predictions fit the training data as well as possible.
A neural network architecture built on attention rather than recurrence, which lets it process all tokens of a sequence in parallel. It underlies modern LLMs.
Flipping a matrix over its diagonal so rows become columns.
How Python treats a value in a condition. Zero, empty containers, empty strings and None count as False; nearly everything else counts as True.
An ordered, immutable sequence, often used for fixed records or returning several values.
A technique that walks two indexes through a sequence, often from both ends or at different speeds, to avoid a nested loop.
Turning a value of one type into another type, such as text into a number. It raises an error if the value cannot be converted.
An annotation that says what types a function expects and returns. Python does not enforce it at runtime; tools and libraries read it.
User Datagram Protocol: a connectionless protocol that sends packets with no delivery or ordering guarantee, trading reliability for speed.
terms.example: used by DNS queries and video calls

terms.definition: When a model is too simple to capture the pattern, so it does poorly on both training and new data.
terms.example: a straight line fitted to a curve

terms.definition: A small automated check that runs one piece of code with known input and asserts the expected output.
Assigning the items of a sequence to several names at once, with * collecting the leftovers.
Finding structure in data that has no labels, such as grouping similar items.
When gradients shrink toward zero as they are propagated back through many steps or layers, so early parts stop learning.
A name that refers to a value stored in memory. Assigning to the name again makes it refer to a different value.
The average squared distance of values from their mean, a measure of how spread out data is.
An ordered list of numbers, seen as a point or an arrow. In ML one row of features is a vector.
Applying an operation to a whole array at once in optimised compiled code instead of writing a Python loop.
terms.example: a * 2  # instead of [x * 2 for x in a]

terms.definition: An isolated folder holding a project's own Python packages, so projects do not clash over versions.
The := operator, which assigns a value to a name and also returns it, so you can use it inside a larger expression.
A human-friendly, indentation-based data format widely used for configuration such as Kubernetes manifests.
How many standard deviations a value lies from the mean: (x - mean) / std.
